'''John David Sutherland''' (born 24 July 1962) is a British [[chemist]] at [[Medical Research Council (UK)|Medical Research Council]] (MRC), [[Laboratory of Molecular Biology]] (LMB), [[Protein]] & [[Nucleic Acid]] Chemistry Division.<ref>
{{ cite web |url=http://www2.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/about-lmb/institute-overview |title=Institute Overview LMB |access-date=9 September 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120904155207/http://www2.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/about-lmb/institute-overview |archive-date=4 September 2012 |url-status=dead }}
</ref> His work on the possible chemistry of early life has been widely recognised.<ref name=":0"/><ref name="www2.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk"/><ref>{{Scopus id }}</ref>

== Education ==
Sutherland obtained a Bachelor of Arts degree in chemistry from the [[University of Oxford]] as a student at [[Lincoln College, Oxford]] in 1984 and a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degree<ref>{{cite thesis|degree=DPhil|publisher=University of Oxford|title=Genetic engineering of penicillin biosynthesis|first= John David|last=Sutherland|date=1988|url=http://solo.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/OXVU1:LSCOP_OX:oxfaleph016062693|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.253132}}|website=bodleian.ox.ac.uk|oclc=53558806}}</ref> supervised by [[Jack Baldwin (chemist)|Jack Baldwin]] at [[Balliol College, Oxford]].<ref name=":0" />

==Career and Research ==
Sutherland lectured organic chemistry at Oxford for eight years. In 1998 he accepted a position at the [[University of Manchester]] as Professor of Biological Chemistry, a position he held until 2010 before moving to Cambridge and the [[Medical Research Council (UK)]] Laboratory of Molecular Biology.<ref>"Curriculum Vitae of John D. Sutherland"</ref> Since 2013, he has been a Simons Investigator and member of the steering committee for the Simons Collaboration on the Origin of Life.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/funding/funding-opportunities/life-sciences/collaboration-on-the-origins-of-life-investigator-award/simons-collaboration-on-the-origins-of-life-john-sutherland/|title=Simons Collaboration on the Origins of Life: John Sutherland {{!}} Simons Foundation|website=simonsfoundation.org|access-date=2016-11-18|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20161118224616/https://www.simonsfoundation.org/funding/funding-opportunities/life-sciences/collaboration-on-the-origins-of-life-investigator-award/simons-collaboration-on-the-origins-of-life-john-sutherland/|archivedate=2016-11-18}}</ref>

In 2009, Sutherland, along with Matthew Powner and Beatrice Gerland, detailed the first plausible prebiotic synthesis of activated [[pyrimidine]] [[nucleotide]]s, which had previously been a significant problem for the RNA World hypothesis of early life emergence.<ref>{{ cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/05/14/science/14rna.html?pagewanted=all |title=Nicholas Wade, "Chemist Shows How RNA Can Be the Starting Point for Life", ''New York Times'', 13 May 2009 |website=The New York Times |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170321194106/http://www.nytimes.com/2009/05/14/science/14rna.html?pagewanted=all |archivedate=2017-03-21 }}</ref> Previous prebiotic syntheses of nucleotides had attempted to form them through assembly of their constituent parts, a nucleobase, sugar, and phosphate,<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last1=Powner|first1=Matthew W.|last2=Gerland|first2=Béatrice|last3=Sutherland|first3=John D.|title=Synthesis of activated pyrimidine ribonucleotides in prebiotically plausible conditions|journal=Nature|volume=459|issue=7244|pages=239–242|doi=10.1038/nature08013|pmid=19444213|date=May 2009|bibcode=2009Natur.459..239P|s2cid=4412117}}</ref> but with only limited efficacy for purine nucleotides, and no success for pyrimidine nucleotides.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Fuller|first1=W. D.|last2=Sanchez|first2=R. A.|last3=Orgel|first3=L. E.|date=14 June 1972|title=Studies in prebiotic synthesis. VI. Synthesis of purine nucleosides|journal=Journal of Molecular Biology|volume=67|issue=1|pages=25–33|issn=0022-2836|pmid=4339529|doi=10.1016/0022-2836(72)90383-x}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=E|first=Orgel Leslie|date=1 January 2004|title=Prebiotic Chemistry and the Origin of the RNA World|journal=Critical Reviews in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology|volume=39|issue=2|pages=99–123|doi=10.1080/10409230490460765|issn=1040-9238|pmid=15217990}}</ref> However, Sutherland produced a synthesis resulting in the formation of β-ribocytidine-2',3' cyclic phosphate, a partially activated nucleotide, that is remarkable for its stereospecifity and yield.<ref name=":1" /> Instead of assembling the nucleotide components in stepwise linear reactions, the synthesis proceeds through the reaction of [[cyanoacetylene]] with an [[2-Aminooxazole|aminooxazole]] intermediate that is formed from [[glycolaldehyde]] and [[cyanamide]], molecules that were likely present on early Earth.<ref name=":1" />

In June 2012, Sutherland, along with his former colleague, the chemist Matthew Powner, from [[University College London]], won the Origin of Life Challenge issued by [[Harry Lonsdale]].<ref name="www2.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk">{{Cite news|url=http://www2.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/john-sutherland-co-wins-the-origin-of-life-challenge/|title=John Sutherland co-wins the Origin of Life Challenge – MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology|date=8 June 2012|newspaper=MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology|access-date=2016-11-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161118224258/http://www2.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/john-sutherland-co-wins-the-origin-of-life-challenge/|archive-date=18 November 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2015, in an article in ''[[Nature Chemistry]]'',<ref name=nchem>{{cite journal | last1 = Patel | first1 = B.H. | last2 = Percivalle | first2 = C. | last3 = Ritson | first3 = D.J. | last4 = Duffy | first4 = C.D. | last5 = Sutherland | first5 = John D. | year = 2015 | title = Common origins of RNA, protein, and lipid precursors in a cyanosulfidic protometabolism | journal = Nature Chemistry | volume = 7 | issue = 4| pages = 301–307 | doi = 10.1038/nchem.2202 | pmid=25803468 | pmc=4568310| bibcode = 2015NatCh...7..301P }}</ref> Sutherland demonstrated [[Cyanosulfidic prebiotic synthesis|a plausible prebiotic scheme]] showing that the precursors of pyrimidine nucleotides formed from [[hydrogen cyanide]] can also form precursors of lipids and amino acids, providing significant evidence that early life may have emerged from a common chemistry on prebiotic Earth.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Patel|first1=Bhavesh H.|last2=Percivalle|first2=Claudia|last3=Ritson|first3=Dougal J.|last4=Duffy|first4=Colm D.|last5=Sutherland|first5=John D.|title=Common origins of RNA, protein and lipid precursors in a cyanosulfidic protometabolism|journal=Nature Chemistry|volume=7|issue=4|pages=301–307|doi=10.1038/nchem.2202|pmc=4568310|pmid=25803468|year=2015|bibcode=2015NatCh...7..301P}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/05/05/science/making-sense-of-the-chemistry-that-led-to-life-on-earth.html|title=Making Sense of the Chemistry That Led to Life on Earth|last=Wade|first=Nicholas|date=4 May 2015|newspaper=The New York Times|issn=0362-4331|access-date=2016-11-18|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170709115606/https://www.nytimes.com/2015/05/05/science/making-sense-of-the-chemistry-that-led-to-life-on-earth.html|archivedate=2017-07-09}}</ref> His work has been heralded by his collaborator and Nobel-prize winning geneticist [[Jack W. Szostak|Jack Szostak]] as an important advance in understanding the origins of life.

He is a proponent of the emerging field known as [[systems chemistry]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Sutherland|first=John|title=Origins of Life Systems Chemistry, John Sutherland, Cambridge|publisher=[[University of Chicago|UChicago]] Physical Sciences Division|format=video|date=2020-11-12|via=YouTube|url=https://youtube.com/watch?v=e5g55ogdvW8}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Sutherland|first=John|title=John Sutherland, Cambridge University, UK {{pipe}} Title: Origins of Life Systems Chemistry|publisher=International Physics of Living Systems|format=video|date=2022-11-10|via=YouTube|url=https://youtube.com/watch?v=AklOtfk8M9o}}</ref>

===Honours and awards ===
* 2009: The Max Tishler Prize Lectureship, Harvard University, USA
* 2011: The [[Tilden Prize|Royal Society of Chemistry Tilden Prize]]
* 2012: Co-winner of the Origin of Life Challenge<ref name="www2.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk"/>
* 2014: The [[Darwin Medal|Royal Society Darwin Medal]]<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www2.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/john-sutherland-awarded-the-2014-darwin-medal/|title=John Sutherland awarded the 2014 Royal Society Darwin Medal – MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology|date=5 August 2014|newspaper=MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology|access-date=2016-11-18}}</ref>
* 2017: Elected [[Fellow of the Royal Society]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/john-sutherland-13427/|title=John Sutherland|publisher=Royal Society|accessdate=2017-05-28|author=Anon|year=2017|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170523130547/https://royalsociety.org/people/john-sutherland-13427/|archivedate=2017-05-23}}</ref>
